es: Revisar un borrador y corregir seis problemas de registro, cohesión y matiz, cambiando lo vago por datos exactos y las afirmaciones exageradas por otras ajustadas.

teaching.en: In a message to the director, a formal register starts with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all.
teaching.es: En un mensaje a la directora, un registro formal empieza con Dear Ms Lopez, no con Hi all.
teaching.explanationEs: Register: el saludo y las palabras deben encajar con quien lee.
segments: In a message to the director, a formal register
starts with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all.
teaching.audioText: In a message to the director, a formal register starts with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all.

teaching.en: A strong claim can overstate the evidence: 'many students seem to dislike it' is more precise than 'everyone hates it'.
teaching.es: Una afirmación fuerte puede exagerar la evidencia: «many students seem to dislike it» es más preciso que «everyone hates it».
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate = exagerar. Sustituye todos/nadie por many/some y añade seem.
segments: A strong claim can overstate the evidence: 'many students seem
to dislike it' is more precise than 'everyone hates it'.
teaching.audioText: A strong claim can overstate the evidence: 'many students seem to dislike it' is more precise than 'everyone hates it'.

teaching.en: A linker such as however or so gives the text cohesion.
teaching.es: Un conector como however o so da cohesión al texto.
teaching.explanationEs: Cohesion: las frases cortas y sueltas se unen con un linker (so, however, although).
segments: A linker such as however or
teaching.audioText: A linker such as however or so gives the text cohesion.

teaching.en: Vague words like soon should become exact details, such as by Friday.
teaching.es: Las palabras vagas como soon deben convertirse en datos exactos, como by Friday.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague = impreciso. Un plazo con fecha es más útil que un adverbio.
segments: Vague words like soon should become
exact details, such as by Friday.
teaching.audioText: Vague words like soon should become exact details, such as by Friday.

teaching.en: To hedge a claim, add seem, may or appear: the price appears to have risen.
teaching.es: Para matizar una afirmación, añade seem, may o appear: el precio parece haber subido.
teaching.explanationEs: Hedge = matizar. Seem to / appear to + verbo suavizan sin perder información.
segments: To hedge a claim, add seem, may or
appear: the price appears to have risen.
teaching.audioText: To hedge a claim, add seem, may or appear: the price appears to have risen.

teaching.en: After you revise a draft, read it aloud and ask whether each change makes it more precise.
teaching.es: Después de revisar un borrador, léelo en voz alta y pregúntate si cada cambio lo hace más preciso.
teaching.explanationEs: Revise = revisar con cambios reales: cada cambio debe mejorar el registro, la cohesión o el matiz.
segments: After you revise a draft, read it aloud and
ask whether each change makes it more precise.
teaching.audioText: After you revise a draft, read it aloud and ask whether each change makes it more precise.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema tiene este saludo al escribir a la directora?

choices.text: Cohesion: it has no linkers.
Register: it is too casual for the director.
Hedging: it is too cautious.

feedback.es: Un saludo informal como «Hi all!» no encaja con un mensaje a la directora: es un problema de registro. No falta ningún conector ni hay exceso de cautela.

hint.es: Piensa a quién va dirigido el mensaje.

origin.text: Draft: Hi all! The director must read this today.

prompt.es: Completa: «A muchos estudiantes parece no gustarles el nuevo menú.»

feedback.es: Seem to + verbo matiza la afirmación: no dice que todos lo odian, sino que parece que a muchos no les gusta.

hint.es: Es el verbo que atenúa: «parece que», no «es seguro que».

origin.text: Many students ___ to dislike the new menu.

prompt.es: ¿Qué cambio sustituye lo vago por un dato exacto?

choices.text: We will ask the director soon.
We will ask the director later.
We will ask the director by Friday.

feedback.es: «By Friday» da un plazo concreto; soon y later son adverbios vagos que no dicen cuándo.

hint.es: Un dato exacto es un día, no un adverbio.

origin.text: Draft: We will ask the director soon.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El menú es nuevo y a los estudiantes parece gustarles.»

answer.text: The menu is new and students seem to like it
accepted: The menu is new and students seem to like it
The menu is new and students appear to like it

feedback.es: El conector and une las dos ideas y seem to matiza la segunda: cohesión y matiz en una sola frase.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dos mejoras tiene la versión editada.

choices.text: A linker joins the ideas, and seem softens the claim.
The register becomes formal, and a date is added.
The ideas are cut, and the claim is stronger.

feedback.es: La versión editada une las frases con and (cohesión) y suaviza con seem to (matiz). No cambia el registro ni añade fechas.

origin.audio: Before the edit: The menu is new. Students like it. After the edit: The menu is new, and students seem to like it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada área de revisión con su pregunta de comprobación.

pairs.es: ¿El saludo y las palabras encajan con el lector?
¿La afirmación fuerte se ajusta con seem o may?
¿Hay datos exactos en lugar de soon?

feedback.es: Cada área tiene una pregunta propia: el registro mira al lector, la cohesión a los conectores, el matiz a la fuerza de la afirmación y lo vago a los datos.

pairs.es: ¿El saludo y las palabras encajan con el lector?
¿La afirmación fuerte se ajusta con seem o may?
¿Hay datos exactos en lugar de soon?

prompt.es: ¿Qué lista resume los problemas principales del borrador?

choices.text: A formal greeting, too many hedges and long sentences.
A casual greeting, overstated claims and a vague time.
A missing thanks, wrong tenses and no title.

feedback.es: El borrador abre con «Hi all», exagera con «everyone hates it» y «obviously» y deja un plazo vago con «soon». El agradecimiento sí aparece al final.

origin.text: Hi all. The school food is terrible and everyone hates it. The new menu is obviously better. Students like it. The price went up. The cooks say they are sorry. We must change the menu now. The director must read this today. We will ask her soon. Last week, two students were ill after lunch. The parents are angry. Nobody wants to wait in a long line. Thank you.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dos áreas mejoró el editor.

choices.text: Cohesion and vague details.
Hedging and vague details.
Register and hedging.

feedback.es: Cambiar Hi all por Dear Ms Lopez mejora el registro, y sustituir «everyone hates it» por «many students seem to dislike it» mejora el matiz.

origin.audio: I changed the greeting to Dear Ms Lopez, and I replaced everyone hates it with many students seem to dislike it.

prompt.es: Completa tres ediciones: conector, plazo exacto y matiz.

feedback.es: However abre el contraste, by marca un plazo exacto («by Monday at the latest») y appears to matiza un dato que no es seguro.

sentences: The price rose; ___, students still seem to like the menu.
Please send your reply ___ Monday at the latest.

prompt.es: Reescribe en un solo mensaje formal: saludo, matiz, conector y plazo exacto.

answer.text: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the school food, so we will ask you to review the menu by Friday.
accepted: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the school food, so we will ask you to review the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, it appears that many students dislike the food, and we will ask you to change the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, some students seem to dislike the school food; therefore, we will ask you to review the menu before Friday.

feedback.es: Un mensaje editado abre con saludo formal, matiza «todos odian» con seem to y many, une las ideas con un conector y fija un plazo exacto.

origin.text: Borrador: «Hi all. Everyone hates the food. We will ask soon.» Reescríbelo como un solo mensaje a la directora, la señora Lopez: saludo formal, matiz en «todos odian», un conector y el plazo exacto (el viernes).

choices.text: The cooks say they are sorry, and they will change the menu.
The cooks say they are sorry. They will change the menu.
The cooks, sorry, change menu.

feedback.es: El conector and une las dos ideas en una sola frase; la versión original las deja sueltas y la tercera elimina palabras sin aportar cohesión.

origin.text: Draft: The cooks say they are sorry. They will change the menu.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué mejoró el editor.

choices.text: He made the register more casual.
He softened an overstated claim and compared it with a fact.
He added a linker between two sentences.

feedback.es: El editor cambió «obviously too high» por «appears to be higher than last year»: suavizó una afirmación exagerada y la apoyó con una comparación.

origin.audio: The draft says the price is obviously too high. The editor changed it to: the price appears to be higher than last year.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de enviarlo, voy a revisar el borrador.»

feedback.es: Revise significa revisar con cambios reales; después de revisar el borrador se lee en voz alta para comprobar el tono.

origin.text: Before I send it, I will ___ the draft.
